items.title: Nvidia’s former sales chief had ties to customers in chip scandal- The Information
items.summary: Investing.com-- Nvidia’s former sales chief Jay Puri served as a key contact for major customers, including Alice Huang, who worked with a Chinese firm that secretly imported at least $7.5 billion of banned Nvidia AI chips into China, The Information reported on Tuesday.

items.title: Nvidia earnings spark after-hours rally in chipmakers, neocloud stocks
items.summary: Investing.com-- Shares of chipmakers and cloud computing firms rose sharply in aftermarket trade on Tuesday after blowout quarterly earnings from sector giant Nvidia helped restore faith in the artificial intelligence trade.

items.title: Earnings Boost Other Chip and AI Stocks
items.summary: Nvidia's peers, customers, and competitors got a lift from the chip maker's solid fiscal third-quarter earnings report, which indicated that demand for artificial-intelligence hardware is still strong.

items.title: Muddy Waters shorts Nvidia, raises questions about possible executive connection
items.summary: Investing.com -- Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is facing another layer of scrutiny as short seller Muddy Waters disclosed a short position in the chipmaker, raising questions about a possible connection between former Nvidia executive Ajay K. Puri and former Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen.

items.title: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) Is An Initial Partner For A New Rack Scale CPU Platform
items.summary: Super Micro Computer (NasdaqGS:SMCI) has been selected as an initial server partner for NVIDIA's new Vera CPU rack-scale platform. The Vera CPU platform is intended to support high performance computing and scientific AI infrastructure for customers worldwide. The German Climate Computing Center plans to use NVIDIA Vera CPUs in a new supercomputer focused on climate and scientific research. items.title: Super Micro Falls 4%, Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Slide 2%: Do New U.S. Export Curbs Deepen Super Micro’s China Problem?
items.summary: Washington just tightened the rules on AI chip shipments, and Super Micro already carries a federal diversion probe. Yet its bigger rivals are bleeding too, which raises a sharper question about who really has the thinnest cushion.
